question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 168 and 14 respectively. If one of the numbers is 42, then find the other number.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The product of two numbers is always equal to the product of their LCM and HCF.

Second Number = (LCM × HCF) ÷ First Number

⇒ Second Number = (168 × 14) ÷ 42

⇒ Second Number = 168 ÷ 3 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of the two numbers = 168

HCF of the two numbers = 14

First number = 42

**Formula Used:**

First Number × Second Number = LCM × HCF

**Calculation:**

Let the second number be x.

⇒ 42 × x = 168 × 14

⇒ x = (168 × 14) ÷ 42

⇒ x = 168 × (14 ÷ 42)

⇒ x = 168 × (1 ÷ 3)

⇒ x = 168 ÷ 3

⇒ x = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM & HCF of Two Numbers

The product of any two given numbers is equal to the product of their LCM and HCF: a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b). This rule applies strictly to exactly two numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime if their HCF is 1. For any pair of co-prime numbers, their LCM is always equal to their product.

Fractions Rule

LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators). HCF of fractions = (HCF of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators).
